chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) judged regarding the foetus of Al-Hilaliya when she was pelted by a rock, so she miscarried what was in her belly, a compensation of a (male) servant, or a (female) servant.

key_terms.غُرَّة: Compensation for a foetus or a single member

ai.seo_question: What is the blood money for a miscarried foetus in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of 'ghurrah' (blood money for a foetus) as a distinct legal category in Shia jurisprudence, derived directly from the Prophet's precedent. It highlights the early recognition of fetal rights and the specific compensation value of a male or female slave, which serves as the foundational metric for calculating diyah in cases of accidental miscarriage due to external trauma.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> judged regarding a foetus of Al-Hilaliya when she was pelted by a rock, so she miscarried what was in her belly, a compensation of a (male) servant, or a (female) servant’.
